Apple___Apple_scab.summary: A fungal disease causing dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Remove and destroy fallen leaves, apply a labeled fungicide at green-tip stage, and prune for airflow.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Choose scab-resistant varieties and avoid overhead irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.summary: A fungal infection producing purple leaf spots and rotting fruit with concentric rings.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out cankers and mummified fruit, apply fungicide during bloom.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitize pruning tools and remove dead wood every dormant season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.summary: A rust fungus that needs both apple and cedar/juniper hosts, causing orange leaf spots.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply fungicide from pink bud through early cover sprays.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts where practical, or plant resistant cultivars.

Apple___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain routine watering, fertilization, and pruning schedule.

Blueberry___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Keep soil acidic (pH 4.5-5.5) and mulch to retain moisture.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.summary: A fungal disease coating leaves and shoots with a white powdery layer.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur or a labeled fungicide and improve canopy airflow.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer and prune for light penetration.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.summary: A fungal disease producing rectangular gray-brown lesions that reduce photosynthesis.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide if disease appears before tasseling on susceptible hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops away from corn and choose resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.summary: A fungal disease forming small reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicide is rarely needed but can help in severe seedling infections.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids; rust severity is highly variety-dependent.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.summary: A fungal disease causing long, cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply fungicide at early disease onset, especially under humid conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops, till residue, and use resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced fertility and scout weekly.

Grape___Black_rot.summary: A fungal disease causing circular brown leaf spots and shriveled, mummified berries.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply fungicide from bud break through veraison and remove mummified berries.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune for canopy airflow and clear fallen debris.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).summary: A trunk disease complex causing tiger-stripe leaf discoloration and berry spotting.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: There is no curative spray; remove and destroy severely infected wood.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid large pruning wounds during wet weather and protect cuts with a sealant.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.summary: A fungal disease producing irregular brown patches that can defoliate vines.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply a labeled fungicide and remove heavily infected leaves.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve air circulation through canopy management.

Grape___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Continue routine canopy management and monitoring.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).summary: A serious bacterial disease spread by psyllid insects, causing blotchy mottled leaves and bitter, lopsided fruit.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy confirmed infected trees to slow spread.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Control the Asian citrus psyllid vector and plant certified disease-free stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.summary: A bacterial disease causing small dark leaf spots and pitted fruit lesions.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide sprays during dormancy and early season.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and avoid overhead watering.

Peach___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Maintain routine pruning and pest monitoring.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.summary: A bacterial disease causing water-soaked leaf spots that turn brown and can defoliate plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based sprays and remove severely infected plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and avoid working in wet fields.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Maintain consistent watering and balanced fertility.

Potato___Early_blight.summary: A fungal disease producing dark concentric-ring spots on lower, older leaves first.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply a labeled fungicide and remove heavily infected foliage.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops and avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.

Potato___Late_blight.summary: A fast-spreading water mold disease causing dark, greasy leaf lesions; historically responsible for major crop losses.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicide promptly and remove infected plants to slow spread.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified seed potatoes and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Potato___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Hill soil properly and rotate planting beds each season.

Raspberry___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune spent canes and maintain good row spacing.

Soybean___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops and monitor for early pest pressure.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.summary: A fungal disease covering leaves in a white powdery coating, weakening the plant.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or a labeled fungicide.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Space plants for airflow and water at the base, not overhead.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.summary: A fungal disease causing small purple spots that merge into scorched-looking patches.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove infected leaves after harvest and apply fungicide if severe.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and renovate beds annually.

Strawberry___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.summary: A bacterial disease producing small dark, greasy spots on leaves and fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide and remove infected debris.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Early_blight.summary: A fungal disease causing dark concentric-ring spots starting on older leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply fungicide and remove affected lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch to prevent soil splash and rotate crops.

Tomato___Late_blight.summary: A fast-moving water mold disease causing dark, water-soaked lesions that can destroy a crop quickly.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply fungicide immediately and remove infected plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and monitor during cool, wet weather.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.summary: A fungal disease common in humid greenhouses, causing pale spots on top of leaves and mold beneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve ventilation and apply a labeled fungicide.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity and avoid overcrowding plants.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.summary: A fungal disease producing many small circular spots with dark borders on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and apply a labeled fungicide.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch, rotate crops, and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.summary: A tiny pest causing stippled, bronzed leaves and fine webbing under heavy infestation.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Apply insecticidal soap or miticide and increase humidity around plants.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Monitor regularly, especially during hot, dry spells.

Tomato___Target_Spot.summary: A fungal disease causing brown lesions with concentric rings resembling a target.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply a labeled fungicide and improve airflow.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Avoid leaf wetness and rotate crops.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: A whitefly-transmitted virus causing upward leaf curling, yellowing, and stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants and manage the whitefly vector.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use reflective mulch, insect netting, and resistant varieties.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.summary: A virus causing mottled light and dark green patterns and leaf distortion.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants and disinfect tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Wash hands and tools between plants; avoid tobacco use near plants.

Tomato___healthy.summary: No visible signs of disease detected.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain consistent watering and staking for airflow.
